title: Put in your first product processes, and keep them light
summary: As a company grows, ad hoc decisions stop working. Add just enough process to keep teams aligned, and drop anything that slows them without helping.

beginner: Ask the team where work gets stuck or repeated.
Pick one problem to fix first, such as unclear priorities.
Try a simple fix, such as a fixed planning cycle or a one-page pitch for new work.
Review it after a few weeks and keep it, change it or drop it.
Write down the process in a few lines.
intermediate: Set a planning rhythm, such as fixed cycles with a short cool-down.
Decide work by how much time it is worth, not only by estimates.
Review processes every quarter and remove what no one uses.
experienced: Design the product operating rhythm for several teams.
Balance consistency across teams with team autonomy.
Coach leads to own and improve their own processes.

canDelegateTo.task: Run the new rhythm and collect feedback

toolExamples.linear: Use cycles to set a fixed planning rhythm.
toolExamples.notion: Write each process on one short page.

sources.title: Shape Up: stop running in circles and ship work that matters (Basecamp)
